text: Gold fell below $3,600 in Asian trade, touching about $3,514, its lowest since September 2025, before recovering to near $3,570; it is on track for its worst week since March.
Silver slipped to about $42.28 by 7:15 AM ET, down roughly 13% this week, a much steeper fall than gold's.
The VIX, Wall Street's fear gauge, rose above 30 before the open for the first time since late March.
Nasdaq 100 futures fell about 1.5% and S&P 500 futures about 0.65%, with Anthropic down over 10% and Intuit down over 10% after cutting its revenue outlook.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell back under 5% to about 4.97% and the 2-year to about 4.70% as money moved into bonds, even though traders still price a December Fed hike as almost certain.
The yen strengthened, with USD/JPY dropping from about 159.8 in Tokyo to near 158.7 in London, below its 200-day average.
Bitcoin slid to about $61,300, its lowest since July, after more than $660 million in leveraged bets were wiped out.
Gold miners and silver funds pointed lower before the open: GDX about 1.4% and SLV about 3.8% below Thursday's closes.
